booklet.title: Sign in from a desktop app through an OIDC provider
booklet.author: Giovanni Porcari

purpose.p: How a desktop app whose interface is a webview on a kajenn server signs a user in through an OIDC provider of _auth (Keycloak, for example), why the sign-in runs in the system browser, what kajenn does and what the desktop app must do.
A source without a repository prefix is a path in the kajenn repository, read on 2026-11-20.

list.item: A kajenn server with _auth, an OIDC provider declared in it, and external_url set.
A desktop app able to stop a navigation of its webview, open a URL in the system browser and listen on 127.0.0.1.

step.title: What happens

diagram.title: Sign-in of a desktop app through the system browser

step.diagram: sequenceDiagram participant W as Webview participant A as Desktop app participant S as kajenn server participant B as System browser participant K as Provider W->>S: GET /_auth/oidc:CODE/start S-->>W: 302 to the provider, state = STATE W->>A: navigation to the provider A->>A: listen on 127.0.0.1, free port A->>B: open the same URL, state = desktop.PORT.STATE B->>K: the user signs in K-->>B: 302 to the server callback with code B->>S: GET callback, state = desktop.PORT.STATE S-->>B: 302 to http://127.0.0.1:PORT/oidc/callback, STATE and code B->>A: GET /oidc/callback A->>W: navigate to the server callback, STATE and code W->>S: GET callback with the session of the webview S-->>W: session with the avatar, 302 to next

list.item: The webview asks /_auth/oidc:<code>/start. The server saves state, PKCE verifier and nonce in the session of the webview and answers 302 to the provider.
The desktop app stops that navigation, listens on 127.0.0.1 on a free port and opens the same URL in the system browser, with the state parameter rewritten as desktop.<port>.<state>.
The user signs in in the system browser. The provider sends the browser to the server callback.
The server recognises the desktop state and answers 302 to http://127.0.0.1:<port>/oidc/callback with the original state and the code, or the provider's error.
The desktop app sends its webview to the server callback with the original state and the code. The server completes the sign-in in the session of the webview and redirects to the next path.

step.p: The system browser never receives the login: the code is useless without the PKCE verifier, which stays in the session of the webview.

step.title: What the desktop app must do

list.item: Recognise the navigation to the provider's authorization endpoint by its own configuration. kajenn adds nothing to the authorization URL.
Read the state of that URL; it is 43 characters of A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -.
On the request it receives, check that state is the original one, then navigate the webview to the server callback with the same state and code.

step.title: Check the server side
step.code:
# A desktop state answers 302 to 127.0.0.1:51001 STATE=$(printf 'A%.0s' $(seq 43)) curl -s -o /dev/null -D - "https://<external_url>/_auth/oidc:<code>/callback?state=desktop.51001.$STATE&code=probe" | grep -i -E '^HTTP|^location'
# A port below 1024 answers 400 curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' "https://<external_url>/_auth/oidc:<code>/callback?state=desktop.80.$STATE&code=probe"

facts.fact: A callback with state desktop.<port>.<state> and code answers 302 to http://127.0.0.1:<port>/oidc/callback?state=<state>&code=<code> with Cache-Control: no-store and Referrer-Policy: no-referrer, exchanges no code and attaches no avatar (tests/auth_app/test_oidc.py, TestDesktopLogin).
The provider's error is passed back in place of code. A port outside 1024-65535, an original state that is not 43 characters of A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -, or neither code nor error answer 400.
The webview sent to the callback with the relayed state and code completes the sign-in in its own session.
